# Configuration

## How configuration works

TTpipe is driven by two kinds of files, as in dietJuicer:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `samplesheet.txt` | One row per sample |
| `config/TTpipeConfig.yaml` | Everything else: reference, switches, processing parameters, DESeq2, GSEA, QC cut-offs |

`--configfile other.yaml` on the launcher replaces it; make that file a complete
copy, because the launcher reads `hpcProfile` and `outputDir` from it. The shipped
file is commented line by line; this chapter is the full reference. No path, name
or parameter is written into the Snakefiles. The defaults reproduce the guide's
workflow unless a comment in the file says "TTpipe change".

```yaml
samplesheet: 'samplesheet.txt'
run_processing: true
run_analysis: true
qc_report: true
results_explorer: true
multiqc: true
multiqc_extra: ''
analysis_counts: ''
hpcProfile: 'profiles/local'
outputDir: 'output'
genome: 'mm10'
genome_fasta: '/path/to/GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa'
gtf: '/path/to/gencode.vM25.annotation.gtf'
star_index: '/path/to/mm10_STARgenome'
build_star_index: false
sjdb_overhang: 100
notify: {email: '', events: ['start', 'success', 'error'], command: 'mail -s {subject} {email}'}
trim: false
fastp_extra: ''
star_extra: ''
min_mapq: 10
remove_duplicates: true
picard_extra: ''
strandedness: 'dUTP'
scale_factors: {}
bigwig_bin_size: 50
bigwig_extra: ''
sample_tracks: false
spike_in: {enabled: false, ...}
htseq_feature: 'gene'
htseq_id_attribute: 'gene_id'
htseq_nonunique: 'all'
count_strand: 'sum'
reference_condition: 'DMSO'
condition_order: []
comparisons: []
design: '~ condition + replicate'
min_count: 10
min_samples: 2
alpha: 0.01
lfc_threshold: 0
gsea_collections: {}
gsea_min_size: 1
gsea_max_size: 1000000
gsea_seed: 42
qc_thresholds: {...}
```

## Samples

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `samplesheet` | `samplesheet.txt` | Path to the tab-separated sample table ([Setup](setup.qmd#samplesheet)) |

## What to run

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `run_processing` | `true` | FASTQ to BAM, tracks and counts. When false, no FASTQ columns are needed |
| `run_analysis` | `true` | DESeq2, GSEA, Sankey |
| `qc_report` | `true` | Per-sample QC table and `TTpipe_qc_report.html` |
| `results_explorer` | `true` | Interactive results page `analysis/TTpipe_results_explorer.html` (volcano / MA, gene search, tables, GSEA tab). Needs `run_analysis`; its padj and log2FC cut-offs start at `alpha` and `lfc_threshold`. See [Differential expression and GSEA](analysis.qmd#results-explorer) |
| `stranded_plots` | `true` | Interactive stranded signal page `analysis/TTpipe_stranded_signal.html`. Built when the stranded bigWigs are made in the run or already exist; skipped quietly in analysis-only runs without bigWigs. See [Stranded signal](analysis.qmd#stranded-signal) and the [next section](#stranded-signal-plots) |
| `multiqc` | `true` | Also `TTpipe_multiqc.html` (FastQC, fastp, STAR, Picard). Only on processing runs |
| `multiqc_extra` | `''` | Extra arguments passed to `multiqc` |
| `analysis_counts` | `''` | For `run_processing: false`: path to an existing count matrix (tab-separated, first column `gene_id`, header = sample `Name`s). Empty = use this pipeline's `counts/counts_deseq2.txt` |

If all of `run_processing`, `run_analysis` and `qc_report` are false the workflow
stops with "nothing to do". With `run_processing: false`, `run_analysis: true` and
no counts anywhere, it stops with a message asking for `analysis_counts`.

## Compute site and output

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `hpcProfile` | `profiles/local` | Profile folder (with `env.sh` and `config.yaml`). Overridden by `--profile` and `$TTPIPE_PROFILE` |
| `outputDir` | `output` | Where results go. A relative path is placed under `$TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT` if set, else the folder you launch from. `~` is expanded. An absolute path is used as written |

## Reference

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `genome` | `mm10` | A label only (shown in the QC report header). Change it to match your organism, for example `hg38` |
| `genome_fasta` | placeholder path (mouse) | Genome FASTA; read only when building the STAR index. **Must match the GTF's chromosome names** |
| `gtf` | placeholder path (mouse) | Unzipped GTF: used by the STAR index, HTSeq and the gene table. Needs `gene` lines with a `gene_id` attribute ([Other genomes](setup.qmd#other-genomes)) |
| `star_index` | placeholder path | STAR genome directory. If empty and `build_star_index` is true: `<outputDir>/reference/star_index`. If empty and the index is not being built, the workflow stops |
| `build_star_index` | `false` | `true`: build the index from `genome_fasta` and `gtf` (once; about 29 GB of memory measured on a mouse genome, 62.5 GB on human GRCh38 plus ERCC92) |
| `sjdb_overhang` | `100` | `STAR --sjdbOverhang` at index build: read length minus 1. Passed explicitly (the guide uses STAR's default, 100) |

The defaults are mouse, but no code is mouse-specific. For human or another
organism, change `genome`, `genome_fasta`, `gtf`, `star_index`,
`sjdb_overhang` and `gsea_collections`; the keys and caveats are in
[Setup: Other genomes](setup.qmd#other-genomes). Mouse has been run on real
data end to end; human (GRCh38, GENCODE v44) has been run on real data for
processing only (no DESeq2 or GSEA).

## Notifications

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `notify.email` | `''` | Address for start, finish and failure emails. `$TTPIPE_EMAIL` wins if set; with neither, nothing is sent |
| `notify.events` | `['start', 'success', 'error']` | Which events send a message |
| `notify.command` | `mail -s {subject} {email}` | Shell command that sends one message; `{subject}` and `{email}` are filled in (shell-quoted) and the body arrives on stdin. Use e.g. `sendmail {email}` and put a `Subject:` line in the body if your cluster has no `mail` |

One email at start, one at the end, one if any job fails (with the last 40 lines
of the Snakemake log); not one per job; none on dry runs. A failure to send
only prints a message.

## Processing

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `trim` | `false` | Trim with fastp before STAR. The guide runs FastQC only |
| `fastp_extra` | `''` | Extra fastp arguments |
| `star_extra` | `''` | Extra STAR arguments (the guide uses STAR's defaults) |
| `min_mapq` | `10` | `samtools view -q`. STAR's unique reads have MAPQ 255 |
| `remove_duplicates` | `true` | Picard `REMOVE_DUPLICATES`; `false` only marks them |
| `picard_extra` | `''` | Extra Picard arguments, e.g. `VALIDATION_STRINGENCY=LENIENT` |
| `strandedness` | `dUTP` | `dUTP` (read 1 antisense, read 2 sense) or `forward` (read 1 sense). Any other value stops the workflow |

STAR is always run with `--outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate --readFilesCommand
zcat --quantMode GeneCounts` and a per-sample `--outTmpDir`; `star_extra` is
added.

## Tracks (bigWig)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `scale_factors` | `{}` | Per-condition overrides, e.g. `{DMSO: 1.2757, 2H: 1}`. Listed conditions use your value; the rest are computed as (largest merged-replicate mapped-pair count) / (this condition's). [Recipe](recipes.qmd#pinning-scale-factors) |
| `bigwig_bin_size` | `50` | `bamCoverage --binSize` (also deepTools' own default) |
| `bigwig_extra` | `''` | Extra `bamCoverage` arguments |
| `sample_tracks` | `false` | Also one bigWig set per sample. [Recipe](recipes.qmd#per-sample-tracks) |

Mapped pairs are BAM records divided by two, on the replicate-merged all-reads
BAMs. `bamCoverage` gets `--scaleFactor` and nothing else for normalisation.
With the spike-in module on, the factors are computed differently (next section).

## Spike-in normalization (optional, experimental) {#spike-in}

Off by default. With `spike_in.enabled: false` nothing changes: the workflow has
the same rules, jobs and commands as without the block. The module is
experimental: it is covered by unit tests and dry runs and has been run once on
real data (human plus ERCC92, processing only, `normalize: ['tracks']`). DESeq2
with spike-in size factors and `size_factor_method: 'genes'` have **not** been
run on real data ([Differential expression and GSEA](analysis.qmd#spike-in)).

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `spike_in.enabled` | `false` | Turn the module on. Needs `run_processing: true` (the spike-in counts come from this run's BAMs) |
| `spike_in.fasta` | `''` | Spike-in sequences, for example `ERCC92.fa` (plain or `.gz`). Required when enabled |
| `spike_in.gtf` | `''` | Optional spike-in annotation, for example `ERCC92.gtf`. An exon-only GTF is fine: a `gene` line is added per `gene_id`. Needed for `counts/counts_spike.txt` and for `size_factor_method: 'genes'` |
| `spike_in.prefix` | `'spike_'` | Added to every spike-in contig name, `gene_id` and `transcript_id` (`ERCC-00002` becomes `spike_ERCC-00002`). No host contig may start with it; the run stops if one does |
| `spike_in.use_contigs` | `[]` | Spike-in contigs (names as in the FASTA, without the prefix) whose reads set the factors. `[]` = all |
| `spike_in.normalize` | `['tracks', 'deseq2']` | `tracks`: bigWig factors from spike-in pairs. `deseq2`: DESeq2 size factors from the spike-in (only when `run_analysis` is true). `[]` = only count the spike-in |
| `spike_in.size_factor_method` | `'total'` | `total`: size factor = spike-in pairs / their geometric mean over samples. `genes`: DESeq2 median-of-ratios on the spike-in genes (`controlGenes`; needs `gtf`) |
| `spike_in.min_pairs` | `10000` | Reserved for a QC warning. Checked to be a number >= 0; not used yet |

An example for ERCC92:

```yaml
spike_in:
  enabled: true
  fasta: '/path/to/ERCC92.fa'
  gtf: '/path/to/ERCC92.gtf'
  prefix: 'spike_'
  use_contigs: []               # or the labeled spike-ins only (see below)
  normalize: ['tracks', 'deseq2']
  size_factor_method: 'total'
star_index: '/path/to/GRCh38_ERCC_STARgenome'   # a NEW directory
build_star_index: true
```

**The STAR index must contain the prefixed spike-in contigs.** TTpipe writes one
combined host plus spike-in reference (`reference/host_spike.fa`, deleted once
the index is built, and `reference/host_spike.gtf`, kept for HTSeq). Either set
`build_star_index: true` with a **new** `star_index` directory, so the index is
built from the combined reference, or point `star_index` at an index already
built from that combined reference. An existing host-only index with
`build_star_index: false` is refused when the workflow is parsed, with a message.

What changes when it is on:

- HTSeq counts on the combined GTF. `counts_forward.txt`, `counts_reverse.txt`
  and `counts_deseq2.txt` hold host genes only, in the usual format; the
  spike-in genes (forward plus reverse) go to `counts/counts_spike.txt` (only
  with `spike_in.gtf`).
- `samtools idxstats` of each final (MAPQ-filtered, deduplicated) BAM gives
  `spike/spike_counts.tsv` (`sample`, `condition`, `host_pairs`,
  `spike_pairs_all`, `spike_pairs_used`, `spike_pct`) and
  `spike/spike_contig_counts.tsv` (pairs per spike-in contig and sample). Pairs
  are mapped records divided by two; `spike_pairs_used` counts only
  `use_contigs`.
- Track factors with `tracks`: (largest `spike_pairs_used` over conditions,
  replicates summed) / this condition's, source `spike-in`. Without `tracks`:
  the usual library-size factor, but on host pairs only. `scale_factors`
  overrides still win. `tracks/scale_factors.tsv` gets two extra columns,
  `host_pairs` and `spike_pairs`. Per-sample tracks use the same basis.
- DESeq2 with `deseq2`: see [Differential expression and GSEA](analysis.qmd#spike-in).

**TT-seq spike-in mixes.** TT-seq kits often add a few 4sU-labeled and a few
unlabeled spike-in RNAs. Only the labeled ones go through the 4sU purification,
so `use_contigs` should list the labeled spike-ins.
Which contigs those are comes from your protocol, not from the reads.

A step-by-step recipe is in [Recipes](recipes.qmd#use-a-spike-in).

## Stranded signal plots {#stranded-signal-plots}

All optional. They control the page `analysis/TTpipe_stranded_signal.html` (see
[Stranded signal](analysis.qmd#stranded-signal)) and have no effect when
`stranded_plots: false`. The page only reads existing outputs; changing a key
reruns just the `stranded_signal` rule.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `stranded_plots` | `true` | Build the page. It needs the stranded bigWigs from this run or from an earlier run in the same `outputDir` |
| `track_loci` | `[]` | Loci to draw: gene symbols (case-insensitive), Ensembl gene ids (with or without `.version`) or `chr:start-end` (1-based, inclusive). Unresolvable entries are listed on the page and in the log |
| `track_top_degs` | `10` | The N most significant genes (smallest non-NA padj) of each contrast. `0` = off. Ignored when the analysis does not run in the workflow |
| `track_regions_bed` | `''` | BED file of regions to draw (chrom, start, end, optional name and strand). The name labels the track |
| `track_max_loci` | `40` | Cap on the number of tracks (order: `track_loci`, top DEGs, BED) |
| `track_flank` | `5000` | Bases added on both sides of the gene or region |
| `track_bin_size` | `100` | Bases per bin (bigWig signal averaged; raised in whole multiples for very wide windows) |
| `track_static_formats` | `[]` | Also write one figure per locus to `analysis/stranded_signal/`: any of `svg`, `pdf`, `png`. Needs matplotlib |
| `metagene_groups` | `['protein_coding', 'lncRNA']` | `gene_type` values for the metagene dropdown (case-insensitive; `all` means every gene; `lncRNA` also takes the older GENCODE types such as `lincRNA`, `antisense`, `processed_transcript`). Groups with fewer than 20 expressed genes are skipped |
| `metagene_flank` | `3000` | Bases either side of the TSS (and of the scaled body) |
| `metagene_min_length` | `1000` | Genes shorter than this are left out of the gene-body view (at least 100) |
| `metagene_bed` | `''` | BED of regions to profile, centre-aligned. A strand column orients them. TTpipe does not call eRNAs; this only chooses where to look |
| `strand_table_min_reads` | `50` | Genes need this many reads (both strands, all samples) to enter the antisense-fraction table; the top 5000 by reads are embedded |

The expressed-gene filter of the metagene reuses `min_count` and `min_samples`
from the DESeq2 section. An example:

```yaml
track_loci: ['Gapdh', 'ENSMUSG00000057666', 'chr1:3000000-3010000']
track_top_degs: 5
track_regions_bed: 'my_enhancers.bed'
metagene_groups: ['protein_coding', 'lncRNA']
track_static_formats: ['svg']
```

## Gene counts (HTSeq)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `htseq_feature` | `gene` | `htseq-count --type`. `gene` counts the whole gene body, introns included: the key difference from an RNA-seq count. Changing it (for example to `exon`) changes the science for TT-seq. (The gene table is always built from the GTF's `gene` lines, whatever this is.) |
| `htseq_id_attribute` | `gene_id` | `--idattr`; also the id attribute `gene_info.py` uses. Change it only if your GTF names the id differently |
| `htseq_nonunique` | `all` | `--nonunique`. `all` counts a read that overlaps several genes for each of them |
| `count_strand` | `sum` | `sum`: forward + reverse per gene (the guide's code). `sense`: forward for + genes, reverse for - genes (the guide's text). [Recipe](recipes.qmd#counting-on-the-sense-strand-only) |

HTSeq is run with `-f bam --stranded no --order pos` on each strand BAM; other
options stay at HTSeq's defaults (for example `--mode union`).

## Differential expression (DESeq2)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `reference_condition` | `DMSO` (in the shipped file; code default: the first condition) | Control `Condition`; the base level and the default reference. Checked against the samplesheet even when `run_analysis` is false, so set it to one of your conditions |
| `condition_order` | `[]` | Order of conditions in plots and the Sankey; must list exactly the samplesheet conditions. Empty = order of appearance |
| `comparisons` | `[]` | `[treatment, reference]` pairs. Empty = every other condition against `reference_condition`. Result names: `<treatment>_vs_<reference>` |
| `design` | `~ condition + replicate` | DESeq2 design. Only `condition` and `replicate` are available; `condition` is required |
| `min_count` | `10` | Prefilter: keep genes with at least this many counts... |
| `min_samples` | `2` | ...in at least this many samples |
| `alpha` | `0.01` | Adjusted p-value cut-off (results and the Sankey) |
| `lfc_threshold` | `0` | `lfcThreshold` in `results()`. 0 = none, as in the guide. Above 0, `stat` changes meaning ([Differential expression and GSEA](analysis.qmd#how-to-read-a-results-table)) |

## GSEA

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `gsea_collections` | `{}` | `{Name: '/path/to/sets.gmt'}`. Empty = GSEA is skipped. Names go into file names. Use gene-symbol sets for your organism (for human, MSigDB files ending `.Hs.symbols.gmt`) |
| `gsea_min_size` | `1` | Smallest gene set kept (guide: 0, no filter) |
| `gsea_max_size` | `1000000` | Largest gene set kept (guide: no filter) |
| `gsea_seed` | `42` | Random seed (the guide uses a time stamp) |

## QC thresholds {#qc-thresholds}

`qc_thresholds` maps a metric to `{direction, warn, fail}`. For
`higher_is_better` a value below `fail` fails and below `warn` warns; for
`lower_is_better` the reverse. A value exactly on a limit is not penalised.

| Metric | Direction | warn | fail |
|--------|-----------|------|------|
| `input_pairs_million` | higher | 20 | 5 |
| `unique_pct` | higher | 70 | 50 |
| `multi_pct` | lower | 15 | 30 |
| `too_short_pct` | lower | 20 | 40 |
| `duplicate_pct` | lower | 40 | 50 |
| `sense_pct` | higher | 90 | 75 |
| `rrna_pct` | lower | 5 | 15 |
| `replicate_correlation` | higher | 0.95 | 0.85 |

The `warn` values for unique, multi, too-short and duplication follow the guide's
rules of thumb; **the `fail` values and the others are TTpipe defaults, not
published standards.** See [Reading the QC report](qc.qmd).

There is also an optional key that is not in the shipped file: `qc_report_banner`
(text shown in a banner at the top of the report; the tests use it to label
synthetic data). The results explorer shows the same banner.

## Environment variables

Set in `~/.bashrc`, outside git (details in [Cluster reference](cluster.qmd#environment-variables)):
`TTPIPE_PROFILE`, `TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT`, `TTPIPE_EMAIL`, `TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT`.

## Deliberate changes from the source guide {#deliberate-changes-from-the-source-guide}

TTpipe reimplements the TT-seq workflow described in a pipeline guide for
Magnitov et al. 2024 (*Mol Cell*, doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2024.11.031; GEO GSE260914;
the authors' code is at <https://github.com/magnitov/zfp143>). It is not the
authors' code. This table lists what TTpipe does differently on purpose; each row
was checked against the code.

| # | Topic | Guide | TTpipe |
|---|-------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Reference | An Ensembl FASTA (chromosomes `1`, `2`, `X`) paired with a GENCODE GTF (`chr1`...), whose names do not match | FASTA and GTF must come from the same source (default: GENCODE vM25 GTF with a chr-prefixed FASTA). TTpipe checks only whether both use a `chr` prefix, on the first sequence |
| 2 | Strandedness | dUTP hard-coded | Config key `strandedness` (`dUTP` or `forward`), checked by the QC report's sense % |
| 3 | Count strand | Text and code disagree | `count_strand`: `sum` (forward + reverse, the guide's code, default) or `sense` (the guide's text) |
| 4 | Scale factors | Hard-coded | Computed, (max / this) over merged-replicate mapped pairs (records / 2); optional per-condition override |
| 5 | DESeq2 variable | `time` | Renamed `condition`; `design` validated; count columns matched to samples by name |
| 6 | VST | `vst()` | Falls back to `varianceStabilizingTransformation()` below 1000 genes |
| 7 | DEG tables | Space-delimited | CSV with a `gene_id` column |
| 8 | GSEA | Java GSEA 4.3.2; time-stamp seed; 10000 permutations; ranked by `gene_id` | fgsea; fixed seed; adaptive multilevel p-values; ranked by gene symbol (largest \|stat\| kept for duplicates). Similar in kind, not identical; never compared here |
| 9 | Sankey | Plotting code not runnable as written | Rewritten to run; a bar chart with one comparison |
| 10 | BAM merges and counting | An extra sort after each merge; one HTSeq call for all BAMs | Merges skip the redundant sort; a one-sample condition is copied; HTSeq per sample and strand (same counts, parallel) |
| 11 | Software and optional steps | FastQC only for read QC | One conda environment per rule group; optional fastp (off by default); optional MultiQC |
| 12 | QC | Not part of the guide | Extra static QC report |

Smaller differences: `--sjdbOverhang`, `--binSize` and HTSeq `--idattr` are
passed explicitly (at the same values as the defaults); STAR gets a per-sample
`--outTmpDir`; `min_mapq` and `remove_duplicates` are config keys; per-sample
tracks, email notifications and the launcher are additions.

**What TTpipe keeps from the guide:** STAR defaults with `--quantMode GeneCounts`;
MAPQ >= 10; Picard `REMOVE_DUPLICATES=true`; HTSeq `--type gene --nonunique all
--stranded no --order pos` on strand-split BAMs; `bamCoverage --scaleFactor`;
DESeq2 with `~ condition + replicate` (the guide's `~ time + replicate`),
alpha 0.01, no log2 fold-change threshold and a prefilter of at least 10 counts
in at least 2 samples; ranking by the Wald statistic; the Up / Down / n.s.
Sankey categories.
